Both records come from your description only. This directory holds the skill library and no project code, hook files or CI history, so I could not inspect either gate.

## Gate 1: integration suite in the pre-push hook

**What I found:** The trial that took the integration suite out of the pre-push hook ended on 10 September with no decision made and no measurement of the red rate. The suite goes back into the hook now (the record calls this REINSTATE). An expired trial defaults to that, and no data exists that could justify keeping it out.

**Why it matters:** For more than two months the trial has had no criterion behind it, so pushes have skipped this check without anyone deciding they should. Changing the date in the hook again would not be a decision.

**Do this first:**
1. Turn the integration suite back on in the pre-push hook. Then push a known-bad change and confirm the hook goes red.
2. If you still want the suite out of the hook, open a new trial. Measure the CI red rate first, give the trial an owner, and make a dated CI step fail at expiry instead of relying on a comment in the hook.
3. Whether this suite should run at pre-push at all is a placement question for `/defect-shift-left`, not for this skill.

**What I did not check:**
- The current hook content: `git log -p -- <hook path>`
- The CI red rate since 3 September: query the CI run history for the integration job
- Whether the hook was ever seen red: look in run history for a failed pre-push run before 3 September

```text
Gate:         integration suite in pre-push hook
Stage:        pre-push (local)
Trigger:      suspended (expiry 10 September passed, no decision)
Proof:        UNPROVEN (no recorded negative control or last red)
Scope:        declared integration suite at pre-push / effective nothing at pre-push since 3 September / delta whole suite unchecked locally
Baseline:     none
Status:       TRIAL (expired)
Decision:     REINSTATE
Guard:        the hook blocks again and its control goes red
Handoff:      defect-shift-left if the suite's stage is in question; a new TRIAL only with red-rate data measured over a defined window
Next action:  remove the trial skip from the hook and push a known-bad change to confirm red
Verification: Not run (no repository available)
```

## Gate 2: deploy gate failing on an identity-provider error

**What I found:** The deploy gate failed on authentication ("application identifier not found in the directory") before it compared anything. It told you nothing about the code. Keep the gate, fix its authentication, then prove it can catch a defect (the record calls this PROVE). An error like this is a gate that could not run, not a failure of what it checks.

**Why it matters:** Deleting the gate because it errored, or because nobody has seen it catch a defect, removes a check without evidence that it is useless. Never having fired means the gate is unproven, not that it is worthless. Until authentication works, deploys either stay blocked or go out unchecked.

**Do this first:**
1. Fix the deploy pipeline's identity: the application ID it uses is not registered in the target directory (it may have been deleted or rotated, or the pipeline points at the wrong tenant or app ID). Rerun the gate.
2. Give "could not evaluate" its own exit code or label so nobody reads it as a defect or as a pass.
3. Run a known-bad target comparison through the gate and record the red run. Because the gate needs target-environment state, pass it to `/defect-shift-left` for 8a.

If the outage lasts longer than delivery can wait, the only allowed loosening is a trial with a measurable criterion, an owner and an expiry that a dated step enforces. Deleting the gate is not an option on this evidence.

**What I did not check:**
- The app registration: `az ad app show --id <appId>` (or your provider's equivalent) against the tenant the pipeline uses
- The gate's red history: the CI run history for the deploy gate
- What the gate compares: read the gate's configuration

```text
Gate:         deploy gate (pre-deploy comparison against target environment)
Stage:        deploy / release
Trigger:      indeterminate (identity provider: app ID not in directory)
Proof:        UNPROVEN ("not catching real defects" = never seen red, not shown useless)
Scope:        declared target-environment comparison / effective nothing this run / delta whole comparison unevaluated
Baseline:     none
Status:       INDETERMINATE
Decision:     PROVE
Guard:        the negative control runs in CI, or its last red run is recorded
Handoff:      defect-shift-left (8a, needs target-environment state); functionality-complexity-tradeoff only if someone argues the obligation itself lapsed
Next action:  restore the app registration or the pipeline's app ID/tenant, then rerun the gate
Verification: Not run (no repository or pipeline available)
```
